strongest_objection: The map's clock-and-phase spine has a factual hole at its most vivid item. Past V1 says a spare standing beside the controls is no use inside the phase, and that is false in every domain the item names: the co-pilot is exactly the spare beside the controls and pilot-incapacitation drills exist to swap at V1, the relief anaesthetist takes over mid-case, the negotiator's second listens on the line so the primary can be pulled. The true mechanism is more useful than the stated one, and strange in the map's own way: the mint is against any party not already following the live state, so the extinguisher is a second in the loop rather than frequent stable states alone, and the distinction from lead-time-floors' Understudy is not that a spare is useless but that a finished-and-waiting spare has not been following. Beneath that, two of the five form claims rest on antecedents the labels do not state. The loop Anchor conditioned on → Last signature → Anchor conditioned on does not close as written, because the last signer is pivotal by place and nobody has conditioned on its name; it closes only where the earlier signers' paper carries a release, a long-stop date, and under that antecedent the loop caps the last signer's holdout instead of buying it the anchor's position, which inverts the label's consequence. The incompatibility Learned your dialect → Switch that reads as a tell is asserted on a case where it fails: a second supplier qualified before a listing is read by a prospectus reader as prudence, not defect, and there is no such move as a second auditor; it holds only where the cure requires a visible transfer of work away from the incumbent inside the window. The items themselves are mostly distinct and none restates power-trades or tollgates-that-must-buy, though the auditor is misfiled under Named in the file (no approval lead time governs an auditor change; disclosure is Switch's mechanism), the utility that must serve under Appearance entered was never replaceable and belongs to tollgates' Hour that must be manned, and the surgeon under Poured foundation has no warranty seam and is routinely replaced by a revision surgeon. I tried to collapse Past V1 into Inside the lead time and Last signature into Kingmaker's tax and could not; both survive by a real separator.

items.item: Poured foundation: the party that did the first phase becomes the only one who can answer for the whole, as the contractor whose foundation is in the ground, the vendor whose first release runs in production, the surgeon who did the first operation on a patient who needs a second, since a replacement can do the next phase but will not warrant what lies under it, and an owner with two parties each warranting half has a defect nobody owns; the dependency created is a single answerable name over work that can no longer be inspected from outside; substitution stops working at the first sign-off the incumbent gives on its own work, because from then on the only inspection of the buried phase is the incumbent's, and it stops for good when re-opening what is buried costs more than what remains of the job; extinguished by a third party's inspection at every phase boundary, bought before the first phase begins so that the record of what lies under the next phase belongs to the owner and a second contractor can accept the seam, or by completion; not who-can-be-bound's Keep the car, where the worker holds the thing until paid, since here the incumbent holds nothing and is pivotal because nobody else will sign for what it did.
items.why: Mechanism is real and distinct (a warranty seam, not a lien), but two parts of the text miss it. The surgeon case has no warranty structure and revision surgery by a second surgeon is routine, so it is the one illustration where a substitute plainly finishes and answers; cut it. The moment is misplaced: the incumbent's sign-off is a document, and a third party can still inspect an exposed footing after it; what closes outside inspection is the next phase covering the first. The extinguisher, inspection at every phase boundary, already assumes this.
items.repair: Poured foundation: the party that did the first phase becomes the only one who can answer for the whole, as the contractor whose foundation is in the ground and the vendor whose first release runs in production, since a replacement can do the next phase but will not warrant what lies under it, and an owner with two parties each warranting half has a defect nobody owns; the dependency created is a single answerable name over work that can no longer be inspected from outside; substitution stops working when the next phase covers the first, because from then on the only record of the buried phase is the incumbent's own sign-off, and it stops for good when re-opening what is buried costs more than what remains of the job; extinguished by a third party's inspection at every phase boundary, bought before the first phase begins so that the record of what lies under the next phase belongs to the owner and a second contractor can accept the seam, or by completion; not who-can-be-bound's Keep the car, where the worker holds the thing until paid, since here the incumbent holds nothing and is pivotal because nobody else will sign for what it did.

items.item: Learned your dialect: the incumbent's skill at this customer's particular work is made by the work itself and can be neither written down nor bought elsewhere, as the supplier whose line runs the part at ninety-eight percent yield after a year while a second source would start at sixty, the paralegal who knows this judge's clerk, the nurse who knows this patient's veins; the dependency created is a yield that exists only in the incumbent; substitution stops working when a substitute's ramp, the scrap and the months at low yield, costs more than what remains of the contract, so the same incumbent is replaceable in year one of a five-year contract and pivotal in year four; extinguished by a second source qualified with a real share of the volume while the first still runs, a tax paid throughout as the price of the pivotality never being minted, or by a design change that sets everyone's yield to zero at once; not Head as the only copy, whose state could be written down and has not been, since here no write-down exists and the extinguisher is a second ramp rather than a document; adjacent to lead-time-floors' Ramp inside the floor, which is the replacement's ramp read as a lead time, since here the ramp the incumbent has already run is what mints it.
items.why: Satisfies the type: replaceable in year one, pivotal in year four, with the threshold named as the ramp against what remains. The extinguisher (second source on real volume, paid throughout) is a genuine cost and not advice. The paralegal who knows the judge's clerk leans toward Voice they will answer, but it is a dialect (how the clerk wants filings) more than a relationship, so it stays.

items.item: Head as the only copy: the process writes its state into one participant faster than it writes it down, as the engineer who knows why the configuration is the way it is, the case manager who has met every witness, the arbitrator who has heard the evidence and watched the witnesses' faces, so the record of the process lives in a head and a substitute cannot resume, only restart; the dependency created is unrecorded state; substitution stops working when the gap between what the head knows and what the file says exceeds what a replacement could recover in the time the process has left, which is why an arbitrator can be replaced after a week of hearings and not after a year, and why most institutional rules let the reconstituted tribunal decide whether the hearings must be repeated; extinguished by the write-down, the handover file, the second engineer who must be able to run it alone for a week, which the pivot resists in proportion to the power it would lose, or by completion; adjacent to status-conversions' Immunity by entanglement, where seniority becomes immunity because the institution's memory runs through one person, since that item reads the conversion of standing and this one the date on the calendar after which the person could no longer be replaced; and adjacent to market-deaths' Wall in one head, where a market's comparison wall is one broker's memory, since here the head sits inside a process still running and can still be copied out.
items.why: The arbitrator rule is the common shape of institutional rules (the reconstituted tribunal decides whether hearings are repeated) and the modality note says so. The separator from Learned your dialect, could-be-written versus cannot-be-written, is real and the author's engineer-versus-operator case proves it.

items.item: Past V1: the process enters a phase that cannot be held still while a replacement arrives, so whoever holds the controls at that instant is the only party who can finish, as the captain past the takeoff decision speed, the anaesthetist after induction, the crane operator with the load off the deck, the tug master inside the lock, the negotiator on the line with the man holding the hostages, the founder in the closing week whose every counterparty has one number in one head; the dependency created is continuity of a state nobody else can take up in motion; substitution stops working at the instant the phase begins, which is usually a named line, V1, the first incision, the load leaving the deck, and works again at the next stable state, the aircraft at altitude on the autopilot, the patient closed, the load on the ground; extinguished by that next stable state, by a protocol that makes stable states frequent and the handover at each rehearsed, which is what the shift handover in intensive care and the negotiating team's rota are for, or by the process ending; distinct from lead-time-floors' Understudy, a spare finished and waiting, since a spare standing beside the controls is no use inside the phase, and this map's question is at which instants the spare can be swapped in.
items.why: The item's central line, that a spare standing beside the controls is no use inside the phase, is contradicted by the co-pilot, the relief anaesthetist, and the negotiator's second, all of whom are swapped in inside the phase precisely because they have been following the state. The repair keeps the mint (a state nobody outside the loop can take up in motion), names the second-in-the-loop as an extinguisher alongside frequent stable states, and corrects the Understudy distinction to what actually separates them: a finished spare that has not been following.
items.repair: Past V1: the process enters a phase that cannot be held still while a replacement arrives, so whoever is on the controls at that instant, together with anyone already following the live state beside them, are the only parties who can finish, as the captain past the takeoff decision speed, the anaesthetist after induction, the crane operator with the load off the deck, the tug master inside the lock, the negotiator on the line with the man holding the hostages, the founder in the closing week whose every counterparty has one number in one head; the dependency created is continuity of a state nobody outside the loop can take up in motion; substitution stops working at the instant the phase begins, which is usually a named line, V1, the first incision, the load leaving the deck, and works again at the next stable state, the aircraft at altitude on the autopilot, the patient closed, the load on the ground; extinguished by that next stable state, by a second already in the loop who can take the controls inside the phase, which is what the co-pilot's incapacitation drill, the relief anaesthetist in the room, and the negotiator's second listening on the line are for, by a protocol that makes stable states frequent and the handover at each rehearsed, which is what the shift handover in intensive care and the negotiating team's rota are for, or by the process ending; distinct from lead-time-floors' Understudy, a spare finished and waiting, since a spare that has not been following the state is no use inside the phase, and this map's question is at which instants, and by whom, the spare can be swapped in.

items.item: Held on their floor: the only copy of a thing the process cannot continue without sits on the replaceable party's premises, as the customer's mould in the supplier's shop, the master tape at the studio, the reference strain in one laboratory's freezer, the source code on the vendor's servers, so the party is pivotal by custody and not by skill; the dependency created is access to an artefact with no second copy; substitution stops working when re-making the artefact would take longer than the process has left, a mould re-cut in months against a launch in weeks, and stops for good where nothing can re-make it, the strain, the negative, the original; extinguished by a duplicate held elsewhere before the dependence forms, the source-code escrow, the culture deposited in a public collection, the tooling clause that names the owner and the right to collect with a truck and a bailiff, and the clause is worth nothing without the truck; not who-can-be-bound's Keep the car, a lien that makes the customer pay the bill, since the mould's holder does not want to be paid for the mould but for every run after it; and not lead-time-floors' Longest-lead part, the slowest component in a build, since here the component exists and is in the wrong hands.
items.why: Custody, not skill, with the moment set by re-make time against time left and the extinguishers (escrow, deposit, tooling clause with a truck) bought before dependence forms. Distinct from Keep the car as the author says: the holder wants the runs, not the bill. Its position in the walk is wrong by the axis; see seriation.

items.item: Named in the file: the process's papers name a specific party where any party would have done, and changing the name needs an approval whose lead time is longer than the process has left, as the manufacturing site named in a drug's marketing authorization, the engineer of record whose stamp is on every drawing, the auditor named in the prospectus, the qualified person who releases each batch, the signatory on the bank mandate; the dependency created is a name in a file a third party keeps; substitution stops working when the third party's change procedure, a variation to the authorization, a new engineer's re-review of every sheet, a board resolution and the bank's six weeks, takes longer than the process has left, so the same name is replaceable in the design phase and pivotal in the month before launch; extinguished by the process ending, by a change pre-approved at entry, a second site already named, two signatories on the mandate, or by the third party's own emergency procedure; not who-can-be-bound's Rented door, where a party buys a place at which to be found, since here the party is written into someone else's process and cannot be written out at that process's own speed; and the party is pivotal without having done anything but be named.
items.why: The auditor named in the prospectus is misfiled: no third party's approval lead time governs changing an auditor before a listing, the company may switch at will, and what binds is that the change must be disclosed for two fiscal years, which is exactly Switch that reads as a tell's mechanism. The same illustration appears in both items; it belongs only to Switch. The repair removes it and adds the discriminator against Switch so the seam is visible.
items.repair: Named in the file: the process's papers name a specific party where any party would have done, and changing the name needs an approval whose lead time is longer than the process has left, as the manufacturing site named in a drug's marketing authorization, the engineer of record whose stamp is on every drawing, the qualified person who releases each batch, the signatory on the bank mandate; the dependency created is a name in a file a third party keeps; substitution stops working when the third party's change procedure, a variation to the authorization, a new engineer's re-review of every sheet, a board resolution and the bank's six weeks, takes longer than the process has left, so the same name is replaceable in the design phase and pivotal in the month before launch; extinguished by the process ending, by a change pre-approved at entry, a second site already named, two signatories on the mandate, or by the third party's own emergency procedure; not who-can-be-bound's Rented door, where a party buys a place at which to be found, since here the party is written into someone else's process and cannot be written out at that process's own speed; not Switch that reads as a tell, where the auditor's name in the prospectus can be changed at will and what binds is that the change must be disclosed, since here the change itself waits on the file's keeper; and the party is pivotal without having done anything but be named.

items.item: Consent that wakes at the exit: a consent right written into a routine contract sleeps for the life of the contract and wakes when the dependent party tries to sell, assign, or refinance, so a counterparty that was one customer among many becomes pivotal to the exit, as the customer whose anti-assignment clause is now on the buyer's list of required consents, the landlord whose lease needs consent to a change of control, the lender whose facility has a change-of-control put, the licensor whose licence does not travel; the dependency created is a veto the pivot did not know it held, since the clause was boilerplate at signing and the pivot learns of its power from the consent request; substitution stops working when the exit process starts, because the contract cannot be replaced without the revenue it carries and the buyer prices the revenue at zero until the consent arrives; extinguished by a carve-out at signing that lets the contract pass on a change of control, by structuring the exit so that no assignment occurs, or by the pivot's own indifference, which is common and cannot be counted on; not term-sheet-powers' Veto priced by the clock, where the investor bought its block over a sale, since here the customer got its block for nothing and did not ask for it; and not Named in the file, where the pivot's name is what cannot be changed, since here the pivot's name is nowhere and its signature is everything.
items.why: Ruling on power-trades: this is the closest collision on the map with an admitted item, power-trades' Veto sold as an improbability, since both are a veto over a named future state priced as improbable at signing. It is not a restatement: there the founder sold the block and received a valuation, here the customer received nothing, did not ask, and learns it holds a veto from the consent request. The item names only term-sheet-powers' Veto priced by the clock, which is the farther neighbor; the repair names both. Also 'prices the revenue at zero until the consent arrives' overstates what buyers do; they discount, escrow, or condition closing.
items.repair: Consent that wakes at the exit: a consent right written into a routine contract sleeps for the life of the contract and wakes when the dependent party tries to sell, assign, or refinance, so a counterparty that was one customer among many becomes pivotal to the exit, as the customer whose anti-assignment clause is now on the buyer's list of required consents, the landlord whose lease needs consent to a change of control, the lender whose facility has a change-of-control put, the licensor whose licence does not travel; the dependency created is a veto the pivot did not know it held, since the clause was boilerplate at signing and the pivot learns of its power from the consent request; substitution stops working when the exit process starts, because the contract cannot be replaced without the revenue it carries and the buyer discounts that revenue, holds it back in escrow, or makes the consent a condition of closing until it arrives; extinguished by a carve-out at signing that lets the contract pass on a change of control, by structuring the exit so that no assignment occurs, or by the pivot's own indifference, which is common and cannot be counted on; not power-trades' Veto sold as an improbability, where the founder sold the investor a block over named future states and was paid a valuation for it, nor term-sheet-powers' Veto priced by the clock, where the investor bought its block over a sale, since here the customer got its block for nothing, did not ask for it, and learns it holds one from the request; and not Named in the file, where the pivot's name is what cannot be changed, since here the pivot's name is nowhere and its signature is everything.

items.item: Sensitized: the dependent party's own history narrows the set of substitutes that can serve it, one exception at a time, until one remains, as the transplant candidate whose prior transfusions and pregnancies have raised antibodies against most donors, the buyer whose ten years of negotiated exceptions mean only one vendor's contract fits its operations, the borrower whose covenants only the incumbent lender will carry, the software estate whose ten years of custom integrations fit one vendor's interface; the dependency created is a compatibility requirement the dependent accreted itself; substitution stops working when the newest exception excludes the last alternative, which the dependent does not notice because each exception was small and won; extinguished by desensitization, a rewrite back to the standard that costs every exception's value at once, by a chain in which the dependent's incompatible match is swapped for another pair's compatible one, as the kidney-exchange chain does, or by a substitute willing to learn the exceptions, which is Learned your dialect begun again; the transplant case is observed and the extension to contracts and covenants is by analogy; not Last one standing, where the field thinned by others' exits, since here the field is full and the dependent cannot use it; and not Head as the only copy, where the state is in the pivot, since here it is in the dependent and the pivot merely fits.
items.why: The dependent as minter of its own hostage-taker is the map's best strange member and the modality is honest (transplant observed, contracts by analogy). The transplant case is not quite 'exceptions won' (pregnancies and transfusions are not negotiated), so the analogy is loose, but it is flagged as analogy and the mechanism, a compatibility requirement accreted by the dependent, is exact.

items.item: Last signature: a process that needs every party's consent and collects the consents one at a time makes the last unsigned party pivotal, whoever it happens to be, as the last parcel in a land assembly, the last creditor in a restructuring without a collective-action clause, the last co-owner of the house, the last state whose ratification brings a treaty into force, the last founder's signature on a round that requires unanimity; the dependency created is a consent that has become the whole deal's condition, since every earlier signature is worthless without it; substitution stops working the moment the count of unsigned parties drops to what the rule requires, one, or the number that completes a threshold, and it never worked for that party's consent in particular but did work for its place, since any of the many could have been last; extinguished by a simultaneous closing in which every signature is held in escrow and released at once so that nobody is last, by a collective-action clause, a drag-along, or a cram-down that lets a majority bind the rest, or by compulsory purchase; not power-trades' Kingmaker's tax, where pivotality is the arithmetic of seats and is traded for ministries, since here it is manufactured by the order of signing and would not exist at a table that closed at once; and not deal-deaths' Signer with no upside, a consent held by someone who gains nothing, since here the signer wanted the deal and is made pivotal by having waited.
items.why: Ruling on power-trades: not a restatement of Kingmaker's tax. The kingmaker's pivotality is computed from seat arithmetic with no sequence and is traded for ministries; here the earlier signers surrendered their vetoes by signing first, so the veto concentrates on whoever remains, and the extinguisher (escrow closing) would do nothing to a kingmaker. The threshold sub-case ('the number that completes a threshold') walks toward the kingmaker's arithmetic, but the item says pivotality is manufactured by order and any of the many could have been last, which is the difference.

items.item: Anchor conditioned on: one party becomes pivotal because every other party's commitment was written as conditional on it, as the lead investor the syndicate's cheques are contingent on, the anchor tenant every co-tenancy clause in the mall refers to, the agent bank the loan syndicate follows, the named principal investigator on a grant, the keynote the other speakers accepted on the strength of; the dependency created is a condition precedent in other people's paper; substitution stops working at the first follower who conditions, since from then on the anchor's withdrawal is not one party lost but all of them, and the anchor learns this at the same moment the followers do; extinguished by closing, which converts every condition into a wire, by a substitute anchor the followers will accept on the same paper, which is rare since the followers were following the name, or by a rule that fixes the followers' commitments to the terms and not to the lead; not Last signature, where the pivot is whoever came last, since here the pivot may have come first and is pivotal because the others tied themselves to it; and not deal-deaths' Champion's single-tender want, where one organization's wanting is held in one sponsor, since here many parties' wanting is held in one outsider.
items.why: Distinct from Last signature by the author's own line: may have come first, pivotal because others tied themselves to it. The principal investigator on a grant is closer to Named in the file (the funder's file names the PI and substitution needs the agency's approval) than to followers conditioning, but the co-investigators do condition on the PI too, so it stays. Ruling on power-trades: Key man's lever is correctly held outside as the paper that prices the passage; the ledger's rejection of it as an item was right.

items.item: Last one standing: the field of substitutes thins by exits that have nothing to do with this process, until the party that remains is pivotal without having done anything, as the last qualified supplier of a component after the others left the line, the last pharmacy that compounds the drug, the last living witness, the last foundry running the old process node, the last firm that still maintains the language the system was written in; the dependency created is the remainder of a market; substitution stops working when the second-to-last exits, which is usually unannounced and often unnoticed by the buyer, whose approved-vendor list still shows five names; extinguished by a lifetime buy that stocks the part for the platform's remaining life, by a redesign that removes the part, by an emulation, or by the platform's own retirement, and the extinguisher's cost rises with every year the attrition went unwatched; a buyer that conceals its sole-source position from the survivor, keeping requests for quotation going to firms that cannot supply, is running walkaway-manufactures' Fed suitor or Qualified on paper against its own pivot, and the concealment holds until the survivor's other customers tell it what it is; not market-deaths' Witness starving, where a benchmark's flow thins to one cargo, since here the thing is still made and traded, and what dies is the buyer's ability to leave.
items.why: Minted by nobody in the process, which the of-sentence's sorting clause admits and its head clause ('an ongoing process makes') does not; see modality. The concealment clause (Fed suitor and Qualified on paper run against one's own pivot) is a real addition and correctly kept as a clause rather than an item.

items.item: Inside the lead time: the time left in the process falls below every substitute's lead time, so the incumbent is pivotal by the calendar alone, as the carrier whose truck is already on the road when the delivery window narrows to a day, the crew that is on site when the harvest is ready, the counsel who holds the brief the week before trial, the fund that has done its diligence when the company has six weeks of cash, the winning bidder after the award when a re-tender would take the whole cycle again; the dependency created is presence inside a window nobody else can reach; substitution stops working at the crossing of two curves, the remaining time falling and the shortest substitute's lead time, and any party that can read both curves can name the day, which is why the union times its strike to the harvest and the port its demands to the peak season; extinguished by the deadline passing, since the power dies with the window it was minted in whether the process finished or failed, by slack restored, a deadline moved, a bridge bought, or by a runner-up held at its bid for the length of the window; adjacent to lead-time-floors' Rising floor, where the lead time lengthens as the runway shortens, since that item reads the dependent party's death line and this one reads what the same clock mints in the hand of whoever is already inside it.
items.why: The crossing of two curves is a real moment and the union-at-harvest case shows the pivot reading it. Extinguishers include the deadline passing, which is the one extinguisher on the map that kills the power whether or not the process finished; that is exact and worth keeping. Its separator from Past V1 is the neighbor test below.

items.item: Float gone to zero: a task that had slack becomes the task the whole project waits on, and its party becomes pivotal, because other tasks finished early or slipped and the critical path moved onto it, as the subcontractor whose ductwork was never on the critical path until the steel came in a month early, the localization vendor whose two weeks became the release's last two weeks, the regulator whose review ran in parallel until everything else was done; the dependency created is a position on the schedule's longest chain, a property of the network and not of the party; substitution stops working when the task's float reaches zero, since from then on every day spent substituting is a day added to the end, and the substitution is itself a task on the critical path; extinguished by the task's completion, which moves the path elsewhere and mints the next party, by re-sequencing that restores float, or by accepting the delay, and a project manager who reads the float report sees the mint a week before the party feels it; not Inside the lead time, where the clock runs out on the whole process, since here the process may have months left and the pivot is made by the shape of what remains; and not lead-time-floors' Chain's longest link, where a replacement waits on other people's replacements, since here nothing is being replaced and the chain is the work itself.
items.why: By the map's own boundary case a party merely more expensive to replace is in only where the replacement's time exceeds what remains. With float at zero and a soft end date, a substitute still finishes, only late, so the item as written admits a delay as a mint. The author's own extinguisher 'accepting the delay' concedes this. The repair makes the hard-date condition explicit so the item passes the fence it draws.
items.repair: Float gone to zero: a task that had slack becomes the task the whole project waits on, and its party becomes pivotal, because other tasks finished early or slipped and the critical path moved onto it, as the subcontractor whose ductwork was never on the critical path until the steel came in a month early, the localization vendor whose two weeks became the release's last two weeks, the regulator whose review ran in parallel until everything else was done; the dependency created is a position on the schedule's longest chain, a property of the network and not of the party; substitution stops working when the task's float reaches zero against an end date that cannot move, a season, a launch slot, a liquidated-damages date, since from then on every day spent substituting is a day past the end, and the substitution is itself a task on the critical path; where the end date is soft the same zero float is a delay and not a mint, which is the line this map draws between costly and impossible; extinguished by the task's completion, which moves the path elsewhere and mints the next party, by re-sequencing that restores float, or by accepting the delay, and a project manager who reads the float report sees the mint a week before the party feels it; not Inside the lead time, where the clock runs out on the whole process, since here the process may have months left and the pivot is made by the shape of what remains; and not lead-time-floors' Chain's longest link, where a replacement waits on other people's replacements, since here nothing is being replaced and the chain is the work itself.

items.item: Voice they will answer: the counterparty's trust attaches to the individual who has carried the process and not to the firm behind them, so the individual becomes pivotal to closing, as the salesperson whose book of business walks with them, the banker the seller will take calls from, the hostage negotiator the kidnappers will speak to and no one else, the diplomat the other side's minister has met four times; the dependency created is a relationship the counterparty will not transfer; substitution stops working when the counterparty declines to speak to anyone else, and it is the counterparty and not the process that fixes that moment, so the mint is made in another party's head and the firm learns of it last; extinguished by closing, by a second voice introduced early and kept on every call, which is why negotiating teams rotate the primary and why a client with two contacts at a firm survives a partner's leaving, or by the counterparty's own turnover; not status-conversions' Furniture's ear or Introducer's tab, which convert standing into access and credit, since here nothing converts and the person is pivotal only inside this process and to this counterparty; and adjacent to Head as the only copy, a record that could be written, since a relationship cannot be written down and can only be duplicated.
items.why: Distinct from Head as the only copy (cannot be written, can be duplicated) and from status-conversions. Ruling on power-trades: Name on the door contains 'the client who will deal only with the named partner', but there the mechanism is a sign regenerating substance after a trade of share, and here it is a relationship fixing the moment inside a running process with no trade; not a restatement. The kidnapper case appears here and in Past V1 as two different mints of one situation, which the boundary claim allows.

items.item: Switch that reads as a tell: the process enters a phase watched by a third party who reads any change of party as a defect in the process, so the incumbent becomes pivotal not because it cannot be replaced but because replacing it would be read, as the auditor in the two years before a listing, whose change must be disclosed in the prospectus, the lead counsel in the middle of a deal, the lead bank before pricing, the chief financial officer before the roadshow, the general contractor while the lender is drawing the loan; the dependency created is the watcher's inference; substitution stops working when the watcher begins watching, which is earlier than the dependent expects since the prospectus reaches back two years, and starts working again when the phase ends; extinguished by the phase ending, by a change announced and explained before the watching begins, a planned rotation on the record, or by the watcher's own rule that names ordinary reasons for a switch; adjacent to lead-time-floors' Seeking is telling, where the source sees the search, since here a third party sees the switch and the dependent's cure for every other mint on this map, qualifying a second source, is itself the tell; and this is the one mint in which the pivot is replaceable and the dependent may not replace it.
items.why: The strangest member that survives: a replaceable pivot the dependent may not replace. One overstatement: 'the dependent's cure for every other mint on this map, qualifying a second source' is false for Held on their floor (escrow), Last signature (escrow closing), Named in the file (pre-approval), and others; the repair narrows it to the commonest cure. The two-year prospectus reach is correct.
items.repair: Switch that reads as a tell: the process enters a phase watched by a third party who reads any change of party as a defect in the process, so the incumbent becomes pivotal not because it cannot be replaced but because replacing it would be read, as the auditor in the two years before a listing, whose change must be disclosed in the prospectus, the lead counsel in the middle of a deal, the lead bank before pricing, the chief financial officer before the roadshow, the general contractor while the lender is drawing the loan; the dependency created is the watcher's inference; substitution stops working when the watcher begins watching, which is earlier than the dependent expects since the prospectus reaches back two years, and starts working again when the phase ends; extinguished by the phase ending, by a change announced and explained before the watching begins, a planned rotation on the record, or by the watcher's own rule that names ordinary reasons for a switch; adjacent to lead-time-floors' Seeking is telling, where the source sees the search, since here a third party sees the switch and the dependent's commonest cure elsewhere on this map, moving work to a second party, is itself the tell; and this is the one mint in which the pivot is replaceable and the dependent may not replace it.

items.item: Appearance entered: the same rule that makes the party pivotal forbids it to price the pivotality, as the attorney of record who cannot withdraw near trial without the court's leave, the physician who cannot abandon a patient mid-course, the utility that must serve, the general contractor whose surety must finish if it walks, the officer who cannot resign in the field; the dependency created is a duty attached at the moment of indispensability, so the power is minted and extinguished in one motion; substitution stops working when the rule's trigger is crossed, the appearance entered, the treatment begun, the service connected, and from then on the pivot is the one party that cannot leave; extinguished before it is born, by the duty, and the duty itself lapses only when a substitute is in place, which is why the court grants leave once new counsel has appeared and the physician may withdraw once the patient is transferred; not tollgates-that-must-buy's Answer that may not be withheld, where the court must decide and the litigant sells it an opinion, since here the rule binds the pivot to stay rather than the gate to buy; and an operator reading the rest of this map should ask at every mint whether a duty attaches, since a pivot with a duty is the cheapest pivot to hold.
items.why: Ruling on tollgates-that-must-buy: the item does not restate it, the pivot bound to stay is the mirror of the gate bound to buy, but one illustration is tollgates' and not this map's. The utility that must serve was never replaceable, so no process minted its position, which is the map's own first tempting nonmember; its duty is Hour that must be manned's compulsion on a gate. The surety case is a duty bought as a bond, not imposed, and the repair says so. 'The service connected' goes with the utility and is replaced by 'the command taken' for the officer.
items.repair: Appearance entered: the same rule that makes the party pivotal forbids it to price the pivotality, as the attorney of record who cannot withdraw near trial without the court's leave, the physician who cannot abandon a patient mid-course, the officer who cannot resign in the field, and the general contractor whose surety must finish if it walks, which is the same leash bought as a bond rather than imposed as a duty; the dependency created is a duty attached at the moment of indispensability, so the power is minted and extinguished in one motion; substitution stops working when the rule's trigger is crossed, the appearance entered, the treatment begun, the command taken, and from then on the pivot is the one party that cannot leave; extinguished before it is born, by the duty, and the duty itself lapses only when a substitute is in place, which is why the court grants leave once new counsel has appeared and the physician may withdraw once the patient is transferred; not tollgates-that-must-buy's Answer that may not be withheld or Hour that must be manned, where the court must decide and the licensed gate must staff the hour and each buys what its position compels, since here the rule binds the pivot to stay rather than the gate to buy, and the utility with a duty to serve belongs there, having never been replaceable; and an operator reading the rest of this map should ask at every mint whether a duty attaches, since a pivot with a duty is the cheapest pivot to hold.

items.item: Discovered by the fire: consolidation several tiers below the dependent party has left one plant or one firm making an input that everyone above it believed came from many, and no party, including the pivot, knows it until the pivot fails, as the 2012 explosion at one chemical plant in Marl that cut off a large share of the world's nylon-12 for fuel and brake lines, and the 2011 earthquake at one microcontroller plant in Naka that stopped car lines on three continents, simplified to the mechanism; the dependency created is a single point in a chain nobody had drawn; substitution stops working years before anyone looks, at the exit of the second-to-last maker two tiers down, and the power is never exercised because it is never known, so the pivot sells at a competitive price a thing it alone can supply; extinguished by the failure itself, after which every buyer maps the tier and dual-sources, and the extinguisher costs the whole platform's downtime instead of a lifetime buy, or by a supply-chain map drawn before the fire, which is the only case on this map where the pivot's ignorance is the dependent's protection and the dependent's ignorance is its exposure; not Last one standing, where the buyer's own approved-vendor list thins in front of it, since here the list is two tiers down and belongs to someone else; and not risk-rebound-effects' mitigations that create a larger risk, since nothing was mitigated and the risk was minted by consolidation nobody chose as a risk.
items.why: Both cases are documented (Evonik's CDT plant at Marl, 2012; Renesas at Naka, 2011) and the mechanism, convergence two tiers down that no buyer had mapped, is right. But 'no party, including the pivot, knows' is too strong for the cases named: Evonik and Renesas knew their shares of CDT and automotive microcontrollers; what nobody above knew was that their many tier-2 suppliers all drew on one plant, and what the pivot did not know was how many buyers that made it sole for. 'Sells at a competitive price a thing it alone can supply' is the map's conjecture (the priority entry admits low confidence in it) and the item should carry that modality itself.
items.repair: Discovered by the fire: consolidation several tiers below the dependent party has left one plant or one firm making an input that everyone above it believed came from many, and none of the parties above it knows, nor often the pivot itself, how many of them it is the only source for, until the pivot fails, as the 2012 explosion at one chemical plant in Marl that cut off a large share of the world's nylon-12 for fuel and brake lines, and the 2011 earthquake at one microcontroller plant in Naka that stopped car lines on three continents, simplified to the mechanism; the dependency created is a single point in a chain nobody had drawn; substitution stops working years before anyone looks, at the exit of the second-to-last maker two tiers down, and the power is never exercised because it is never known, so the pivot sells, on this map's conjecture, at a competitive price a thing it alone can supply; extinguished by the failure itself, after which every buyer maps the tier and dual-sources, and the extinguisher costs the whole platform's downtime instead of a lifetime buy, or by a supply-chain map drawn before the fire, which is the only case on this map where the pivot's ignorance of its buyers is the dependent's protection and the dependent's ignorance of its tiers is its exposure; not Last one standing, where the buyer's own approved-vendor list thins in front of it, since here the list is two tiers down and belongs to someone else; and not risk-rebound-effects' mitigations that create a larger risk, since nothing was mitigated and the risk was minted by consolidation nobody chose as a risk.

neighbor_test.left: Past V1: the process enters a phase that cannot be held still while a replacement arrives, so whoever holds the controls at that instant is the only party who can finish, as the captain past the takeoff decision speed, the anaesthetist after induction, the crane operator with the load off the deck, the tug master inside the lock, the negotiator on the line with the man holding the hostages, the founder in the closing week whose every counterparty has one number in one head; the dependency created is continuity of a state nobody else can take up in motion; substitution stops working at the instant the phase begins, which is usually a named line, V1, the first incision, the load leaving the deck, and works again at the next stable state, the aircraft at altitude on the autopilot, the patient closed, the load on the ground; extinguished by that next stable state, by a protocol that makes stable states frequent and the handover at each rehearsed, which is what the shift handover in intensive care and the negotiating team's rota are for, or by the process ending; distinct from lead-time-floors' Understudy, a spare finished and waiting, since a spare standing beside the controls is no use inside the phase, and this map's question is at which instants the spare can be swapped in.
neighbor_test.right: Inside the lead time: the time left in the process falls below every substitute's lead time, so the incumbent is pivotal by the calendar alone, as the carrier whose truck is already on the road when the delivery window narrows to a day, the crew that is on site when the harvest is ready, the counsel who holds the brief the week before trial, the fund that has done its diligence when the company has six weeks of cash, the winning bidder after the award when a re-tender would take the whole cycle again; the dependency created is presence inside a window nobody else can reach; substitution stops working at the crossing of two curves, the remaining time falling and the shortest substitute's lead time, and any party that can read both curves can name the day, which is why the union times its strike to the harvest and the port its demands to the peak season; extinguished by the deadline passing, since the power dies with the window it was minted in whether the process finished or failed, by slack restored, a deadline moved, a bridge bought, or by a runner-up held at its bid for the length of the window; adjacent to lead-time-floors' Rising floor, where the lead time lengthens as the runway shortens, since that item reads the dependent party's death line and this one reads what the same clock mints in the hand of whoever is already inside it.
neighbor_test.separating_case: These are the two closest because Past V1 is the limit of Inside the lead time where the time left is seconds, and both are minted by the clock alone. Case: one harbour pilot, two days. Day one, the pilot boards at the station with the tide window closing in forty minutes and no other pilot within reach; the pilot is pivotal by Inside the lead time, and the power dies either way at the window, since the ship can drop anchor and wait twelve hours for the next tide, which is the extinguisher 'deadline moved'. Day two, the same pilot is conning the ship in the channel with the tide falling; there is no state in which the ship can be held still, no anchorage in the channel, and no next tide to wait for, so the pilot is pivotal by Past V1 and the power dies only at the berth. The separator is whether anyone can restore slack: on day one a wait restores it and the window's passing extinguishes the power whether or not the ship got in; on day two nothing restores it and the window cannot pass, since the phase must end in a berth or a grounding. And on day two the second pilot on the bridge who has been watching the marks can take the con, which is the repaired Past V1's extinguisher and has no counterpart on day one, where a second pilot at the station is as far away as the first. The items do not collapse.

boundary_case: The only eyewitness against the last living witness. The last living witness is on the map under Last one standing, pivotal because the others died; the only eyewitness, who alone saw the event, is the tempting nonmember and is out, since there was never a second and no process minted the position; the map's fence is the transition. A second tempting nonmember is the vendor whose contract carries a large early-termination fee: leaving is expensive and the fee grows with what remains, which looks like a mint on the clock, but the fee was a priced term agreed at entry, a substitute can finish, and the vendor holds only what who-can-be-bound's paper gave it, so it is out unless the fee exceeds what remains of the process, which is the map's own threshold and not a new mechanism. The of-sentence's head clause needs one word changed to hold its own members: 'an ongoing process makes' is contradicted by Last one standing and Discovered by the fire, which the sorting clause admits under the market's leaving and 'nobody'; read it as 'during an ongoing process, a previously replaceable party becomes indispensable'.

seriation.note: The axis (who mints) is real and the endpoints are placed for the right reasons: Poured foundation is minted by the incumbent's own hands and priced at the next phase, Discovered by the fire by nobody and never priced. One ordering slip: the axis sentence runs 'hands, head, or custody, then the work's own phases', but the itinerary puts Past V1 (a phase) before Held on their floor (custody). Move Held on their floor ahead of Past V1, or amend the axis; the former is cleaner because it keeps the three incumbent mints contiguous. The claimed consequential adjacencies hold: Learned your dialect → Head as the only copy separates on the extinguisher (a ramp paid throughout against a document), and Named in the file → Consent that wakes → Sensitized is a genuine walk through the dependent's own paper, though after the repair the auditor no longer appears in Named in the file and the seriation note's claim that the dependent 'writes the pivot's name into a third party's file' should be read on the manufacturing site and the engineer of record. The end of the walk, watcher → rule → nobody, is where the axis runs out and the note says so honestly.

edges.why: The passage is real but the antecedent is missing a condition. In a venture round or a loan syndicate the last follower can hold the anchor's syndicate only if the closing needs all followers or a minimum the last cheque completes; where the round can close short or the allocation can be filled from outside, the last follower holds nothing. Co-tenancy clauses condition on the anchor, not on every tenant, so in the mall case the edge does not fire at all. The label should state the condition so the antecedent can fail.
edges.repair_label: If the anchor has committed, the followers' consents are collected one at a time, and the closing needs all of them or a minimum the last cheque completes, the closing runs down to a last follower who can now hold the anchor's whole syndicate, so the party that conditioned on the anchor inherits the anchor's pivotality by arriving last; where the round can close short or the allocation can be filled from outside, the last follower holds nothing, and a simultaneous closing that cures the last signature cures the anchor only if the anchor's own wire sits in the same escrow.

edges.why: As written the loop conflates being waited on with being conditioned on. Anchor's mark is that the followers' paper conditions on the anchor's name, so its withdrawal releases them; the last signer is pivotal by place, nobody conditioned on its name, and the earlier signers are not released by its refusal, which is exactly why it can hold them. Becoming known does not change this and often weakens the last signer, since a known holdout can be routed around. The loop closes only where the earlier signers' commitments carry a release, a long-stop date, and under that antecedent the consequence inverts: the last signer's refusal frees everyone, which caps its holdout at the deal's value to itself before the date, rather than buying it the anchor's position. That is a real conditional claim and a better inference than the one the author drew.
edges.repair_label: If the earlier signers' commitments carry a release, a long-stop date or a condition that their consent lapses unless the last party signs by it, the last signer's refusal does not hold them but frees them, which is the anchor's shape, every other commitment conditioned on one party, so the loop closes and what the last signer holds is capped at the deal's value to itself before the date; where the earlier signatures are unconditional and undated, nobody has conditioned on the last signer's name, it holds everyone by place alone, the loop does not close, and arriving late on purpose buys the holdout and not the anchor's position.

edges.why: A true fork with a failing antecedent: followers who conditioned on the institution leave the person replaceable inside it. Key man's lever is the LP-to-GP paper for the same passage and is cited, not restated.

edges.to_handle: Switch that reads as a tell
edges.why: The incompatibility is asserted on the case where it fails. Qualifying a second supplier before a listing is read by a prospectus reader as prudence, and single-source dependence is what appears as a risk factor; and 'a second auditor' is not a move anyone makes. The incompatibility holds where the cure requires a visible transfer of work away from the incumbent inside the watched window, as moving a lead counsel's brief mid-deal or a general contractor's scope while the lender is drawing, and fails where the second source can be added without the incumbent's share visibly falling. The narrowed edge still supports the form inference's conditional incompatibility.
edges.repair_label: If the process has entered a watched phase and the learned yield's only extinguisher, a second source run on a real share of the volume, requires a visible transfer of work away from the incumbent inside the window, as moving a lead counsel's brief mid-deal or a general contractor's scope while the lender is drawing, the transfer is the tell the watcher reads as a defect in the first, so the cure is unavailable exactly when the mint bites; where the second source can be added without the incumbent's share visibly falling, or the watcher reads dual-sourcing as prudence, as a prospectus reader does with a supplier, both stand and the dual-source tax works.

edges.why: A real dependency with a failing antecedent: the same visible state, one substitute left, has its cure on the dependent's side or the market's, and the label names both roads. The lifetime buy does not apply to the covenant or software cases, but the general point, that the search is the wrong extinguisher for a sensitized position, holds.

One mechanism, the second-to-last exit, forked by whose list it happens on; the antecedent (the buyer does not keep the list to that tier) can fail and the consequence (priced at negotiation versus paid in downtime) follows. After the item repair, 'nobody can see' should be read as nobody above the pivot.

A dependency with a real failing antecedent: the law attaches the duty only to phases it has named, and the founder in the closing week and the engineer on the cutover night are unnamed and may price. The captain and the surgeon are pivotal and bound in one motion. The repaired Past V1 does not disturb this edge.

modality_problems: Past V1: 'a spare standing beside the controls is no use inside the phase' is false in every named domain (co-pilot incapacitation drills at V1, relief anaesthetists, the negotiator's second on the line); repaired to a second-in-the-loop extinguisher.

Named in the file: the auditor named in the prospectus is not held by an approval lead time; the company may switch at will and must disclose for two fiscal years, which is Switch that reads as a tell's mechanism; the same illustration sat in both items; repaired by removal.

Appearance entered: the utility that must serve was never replaceable and fails the map's own fence; its duty is tollgates-that-must-buy's Hour that must be manned; repaired by removal and by naming the surety as a duty bought rather than imposed.
Poured foundation: the surgeon has no warranty seam and is routinely replaced by a revision surgeon; the moment is the covering-over, not the sign-off; repaired.
Consent that wakes at the exit: 'the buyer prices the revenue at zero until the consent arrives' overstates; buyers discount, escrow, or condition closing; repaired.

Discovered by the fire: 'no party, including the pivot, knows' is stronger than the Marl and Naka cases support, since Evonik and Renesas knew their shares; what was unknown was the convergence above; 'sells at a competitive price' is conjecture and now says so; repaired.
Switch that reads as a tell: 'the dependent's cure for every other mint on this map' is false for at least four items; repaired to 'commonest cure'.
Float gone to zero: with a soft end date the item admits a delay as a mint, against the map's own boundary case; repaired with the hard-date condition.
Edge Learned your dialect → Switch: a second supplier qualified before a listing is read as prudence, and 'a second auditor' is not a real move; repaired to the visible-transfer antecedent.
Edge Last signature → Anchor: the loop conflates being waited on with being conditioned on; repaired to the long-stop antecedent, under which the consequence inverts to a cap.

The of-sentence's head clause, 'an ongoing process makes', is contradicted by Last one standing and Discovered by the fire, which its own sorting clause admits under the market's leaving and 'nobody'; one-word repair suggested in boundary_case, left to the repairer since it is outside the item schema.
best_unresolved_seed: Who learns the mint first, and what the interval buys. Across the map the pivot learns before the dependent (Head as the only copy, Learned your dialect, where the pivot resists the write-down in proportion to what it would lose), the dependent learns before the pivot (Consent that wakes, where the pivot learns from the request; Float gone to zero, where the float report shows the mint a week before the party feels it), both learn at once (Anchor conditioned on), or neither learns until failure (Discovered by the fire). The party that sees the mint first can buy the extinguisher at pre-mint prices, which is the whole value of seeing it; the map contains the extinguishers but not the ordering of knowledge, and the ledger's residue seed, a pivot that refuses to be minted by building its own extinguisher in advance, is the pivot-side half of the same list. A map of mint-knowledge orderings, with what each interval lets the first knower buy and what the counterparty reads into a party that keeps itself replaceable, is the next expedition.
independent_review_line: Fable critic: admitted after repairing eight items and three edge labels, chiefly Past V1's false claim that a spare beside the controls is no use inside the phase, the auditor misfiled under Named in the file, the never-replaceable utility under Appearance entered, and the anchor-last-signer loop and dialect-tell incompatibility narrowed to the antecedents under which they hold; Held on their floor moved ahead of Past V1 to match the axis; no item restates power-trades or tollgates-that-must-buy.
